Synopsis:
MMF assets hit a record $13.5T globally (~$8T US), up 58-65% since Dec 2022. The original rate-driven inflow thesis has evolved: MMFs are no longer just a yield play but a structural strategic allocation. Institutional flight-to-safety amid macro/geopolitical uncertainty and a massive new corporate cash overhang — driven by AI-related capital raises exceeding $300B+ across 2025-2026 — are now the dominant flow drivers. This distinction matters critically: if MMFs are strategic/structural rather than parked "dry powder," the assumed rotation into risk assets upon rate cuts may not materialize at scale.
